content:
According to Bloomberg's latest report, Apple will launch a brand-new "Apple Upgrade" leasing programme in the United States at the end of this month. The report describes this move as "one of the biggest changes ever to how the company sells devices."

Here's how it works.

Reducing the monthly instalment amount for hardware purchases

Apple will partner with Klarna to support the new Apple Upgrade programme. Consumers will need to undergo a soft credit check when applying.

Apple Upgrade is reported to operate "similar to a subscription service" and applies to purchases of iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch. However, there are certain restrictions on the programme. Reports indicate that Apple Watch SE, the basic iPad, iPhone 16, and MacBook Neo are all ineligible for Apple Upgrade.

The lease term for iPhone and Apple Watch is reportedly 24 months, while for Mac it is 36 months.

Mark Gurman explains as follows:

Unlike the iPhone Upgrade Program, Apple Upgrade does not include AppleCare coverage. In fact, Bloomberg noted that Apple plans to stop new enrolments for the iPhone Upgrade Program as Apple Upgrade launches.

Apple Upgrade is reported to officially launch a week from today, that is, 28 July.

Apple raised iPad and Mac prices last month, and the new iPhone expected in September is also forecast to see a price hike. Apple Upgrade will provide customers with an option to cope with the price increases.
